mainTopic: Two hairs as the sign of adulthood: חליצה and מצוות, בן סורר ומורה, the limits of מיאון, and the rules about follicles
overview: A new משנה teaches that growing two hairs is the sign of adulthood. A girl with two hairs does חליצה or יבום and is obligated in all the מצוות. A boy with two hairs is obligated in all the מצוות and can be a בן סורר ומורה until his lower 'beard' forms a circle. A girl with two hairs can no longer do מיאון, but רבי יהודה says she keeps that right until the black hair is the majority. The גמרא explains why the משנה spells out חליצה and יבום: to reject רבי יוסי. It explains that the boy's section is written only to match the girl's. It then rules like רבי יהודה, but even he agrees that she loses מיאון once she is with her husband after two hairs. Two stories show the חכמים refusing to allow מיאון in that case. The גמרא then defines the two hairs: they need follicles, and follicles alone can count. It also sorts out two sages with similar names, רב מלכיו and רב מלכיא. Finally, it asks whether two hairs can really grow from one follicle, using a פסוק in איוב, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing word of the previous discussion
steps.stepSummary: The single word רֵיחָנֵי (fragrant spices) is the end of the discussion that came before this משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...fragrant spices.
steps.whatsHappening: This one word finishes the earlier discussion about spices. It is not part of the new topic, and the new משנה starts right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The page break fell in the middle of the earlier sugya, so its last word shows up here. Nothing new is taught in this word for our topic. It just closes what came before.

keyTerms.meaning: Fragrant things, meaning sweet-smelling spices

steps.confusionAlert: Don't try to connect this word to the משנה about two hairs. It belongs to the previous discussion.

phrases.english: fragrant spices.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier sugya, which runs in from the previous page.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: End of the earlier discussion about spices. No new teaching here for the coming משנה.

steps.title: A girl with two hairs is an adult
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a girl who has grown two hairs is an adult. She can do חליצה or יבום, and she is obligated in all the מצוות of the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A young girl who has grown two hairs either does חליצה or does יבום, and she is obligated in all the מצוות stated in the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says that growing two hairs is the sign that a girl has become a full adult in הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this sign, she is treated as a child. Once she grows two hairs, two things change. If her husband died without children, she now does real יבום or חליצה. She is also now responsible for all the מצוות that apply to women.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, meaning 'our משנה'. It marks where the משנה begins.
Two hairs, the physical sign of adulthood
A young girl
Does חֲלִיצָה, the ceremony that releases a childless widow from her brother-in-law
Marries her late husband's brother through יִבּוּם

steps.whyThisMatters: Two hairs is the basic sign of adulthood used all across הלכה. It decides when a person becomes fully responsible for מצוות.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
A young girl who grew two hairs,
phrases.notes: These are the hairs of puberty, the body's sign of adulthood.

phrases.english: either does chalitzah or does yibum,
and she is obligated in all the מצוות stated in the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A girl with two hairs is an adult: she does חליצה or יבום and is obligated in all the מצוות.

steps.title: A boy with two hairs is an adult, and the window for being a rebellious son
steps.stepSummary: A boy with two hairs is obligated in all the מצוות. He can be judged as a בן סורר ומורה from the time he grows two hairs until his 'beard forms a circle'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise, a young boy who has grown two hairs is obligated in all the מצוות stated in the Torah. He can be judged as a בן סורר ומורה from when he grows two hairs until his beard forms a circle.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the same rule for a boy: two hairs make him an adult. It then adds a special law about the בן סורר ומורה (the rebellious son).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being an adult makes the boy responsible for all the מצוות. The law of בן סורר ומורה applies only during a short window. It starts when he grows two hairs and ends when 'his beard forms a circle.' The next step explains what that phrase means.

keyTerms.meaning: A young boy
The 'stubborn and rebellious son' of the Torah, who is judged by בית דין
Fit to be, meaning he is able to be judged as one
Until the beard forms a circle, which marks the end of the window

steps.confusionAlert: Being an adult does not mean a boy can be a בן סורר ומורה forever. There is an end point too, and the next line explains it.

phrases.english: And likewise, a young boy who grew two hairs
is obligated in all the מצוות stated in the Torah,
and he is fit to be a stubborn and rebellious son
from when he grows two hairs
until his beard forms a circle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the same adulthood rule for a boy and adds the time window for בן סורר ומורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A boy with two hairs is obligated in all the מצוות, and he can be a בן סורר ומורה only from two hairs until his 'beard' forms a circle.

steps.title: 'Beard' means the lower hair, said politely
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains that the 'beard' it mentioned is the lower hair, not the face. The חכמים used a polite, clean way of speaking.
steps.simpleTranslation: The lower one, and not the upper one. It is only that the חכמים spoke in clean language.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains its own word 'beard' so nobody thinks it means facial hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the בן סורר ומורה window depends on the lower (pubic) hair filling out in a circle, not on a beard growing on the face. The חכמים called it 'beard' only to avoid saying something immodest. That is why the משנה has to clarify it.

keyTerms.meaning: The lower one, meaning the lower (pubic) hair
The upper one, meaning the facial beard
Clean language, a polite way of saying something sensitive

steps.whatToRemember: Two hairs make a girl or boy an adult in הלכה. For a boy, the בן סורר ומורה window runs from two hairs until the lower hair forms a circle. 'Beard' here is a polite word for the lower hair.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'beard' as facial hair. The משנה itself says it means the lower hair.

phrases.english: The lower one, and not the upper one,
phrases.notes: He means the lower 'beard', the pubic hair, not the beard on the face.

phrases.english: it is only that the Sages spoke
in clean language.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what the word 'beard' means in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'beard' that ends the בן סורר ומורה window is the lower hair. The חכמים called it 'beard' to speak politely.

steps.title: A girl with two hairs can no longer do מיאון
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that once a girl has grown two hairs, she can no longer end her marriage through מיאון. רבי יהודה says she keeps that right until the black hair is the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: A young girl who has grown two hairs can no longer do מיאון. רבי יהודה says she can still do it until the black hair becomes the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more result of growing two hairs: a girl loses her right to do מיאון. רבי יהודה disagrees about exactly when that happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מיאון only works for a girl who is still a קטנה. The תנא קמא says two hairs are enough to make her an adult, so מיאון is over. רבי יהודה holds she still counts as young for this purpose until the black hair is the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: To refuse. This means to do מיאון.
Refusal. A girl married off as a minor by her mother or brothers can walk out of the marriage by refusing.
A young girl.
Until the black becomes the majority, meaning the dark hair covers most of the area.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up מיאון with a גט. מיאון is not a divorce. It is the girl's own refusal of a marriage that was only מדרבנן, and it is only open to her while she is still a קטנה.

phrases.english: A young girl who has grown two hairs,
cannot refuse.
phrases.notes: Refusing here is מיאון: a girl married off as a child can leave that marriage just by refusing it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
until the black becomes the majority.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינוֹקֶת שֶׁהֵבִיאָה שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת, אֵינָהּ יְכוֹלָה לְמַאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of what changes once a child grows two hairs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two hairs end a girl's right to do מיאון. רבי יהודה says the right lasts until the black hair is the majority.

steps.title: Why mention חליצה and יבום separately?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה lists חליצה and יבום for the girl when it already said she is obligated in all the מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא asks: since the משנה already said she is obligated in all the מצוות of the Torah, why did it also need to say she does חליצה or יבום?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by pointing out what looks like extra words in the משנה (from Step 2).
steps.deeperAnalysis: חליצה and יבום are themselves מצוות of the Torah. So 'obligated in all the מצוות' should already include them. The גמרא wants to know what these extra words teach.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the אמוראים on the משנה.
Why do I need it? This asks why something extra was written.
She does חליצה.
She is married through יבום.

phrases.english: GEMARA: And since we learned
"she is obligated in all the מצוות stated in the Torah,"
why do I need "she either does chalitzah or enters yibum"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה to the גמרא's first question about the משנה's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's separate mention of חליצה and יבום in Step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Repetition: the general phrase 'all the מצוות' already includes חליצה and יבום.

steps.title: The extra words reject רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The extra words teach against רבי יוסי, who said a girl can do חליצה even as a minor. Really, she needs two hairs, because a woman is compared to a man.
steps.simpleTranslation: The extra words come to reject רבי יוסי. He said the פסוק only says 'man', so the man must be an adult, but the woman can be adult or minor. The משנה teaches that if she grew two hairs, yes, and if not, no. Why? A woman is like a man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extra words are there to argue with רבי יוסי about the age of a woman doing חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי read the word 'man' in the פרשה as limiting only the man to an adult, leaving the woman at any age. The משנה disagrees and requires two hairs for her too. The reason is that the woman is compared to the man: just as he must be an adult, so must she.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, meaning to reject another opinion.
The section of the Torah, here the פרשה of חליצה.
It teaches us. This introduces the new lesson.
What is the reason?
A woman is like a man. Her rule follows his rule.

steps.whatToRemember: The words 'חליצה or יבום' are not extra. They teach that a girl needs two hairs for חליצה, against רבי יוסי, because a woman is compared to a man.

phrases.english: To exclude the view of Rabbi Yosei,
who said: "man" is written in the section,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אִשָּׁה, בֵּין גְּדוֹלָה וּבֵין קְטַנָּה.
phrases.english: but a woman, whether adult or minor.
It teaches us
that if she grew two hairs, yes,
if not, no.
What is the reason? A woman is like a man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The extra words come to reject a different opinion (רבי יוסי).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following רבי יוסי, a girl could do חליצה even before growing two hairs.
steps.terutzMaskana: A girl needs two hairs to do חליצה or יבום, because a woman is compared to a man.

steps.title: Same question about the boy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה says the boy is obligated in all the מצוות, when it already said 'and likewise' about him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since the משנה said 'and likewise a boy who grew two hairs', why do I need it to add that he is obligated in all the מצוות of the Torah?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a similar question about the boy's part of the משנה (Step 3). Step 9 blocks one possible answer, and step 10 gives the real answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וכן' (and likewise) already puts the boy into the same rules as the girl. So spelling out 'obligated in all the מצוות' for him again looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise. It shows the same rule applies here too.
A young boy.

phrases.english: And since it taught
"and likewise a young boy who grew two hairs,"

phrases.aramaic: ״חַיָּיב בְּכׇל הַמִּצְוֹת הָאֲמוּרוֹת בַּתּוֹרָה״ לְמָה לִי?
phrases.english: why do I need "he is obligated in all the מצוות stated in the Torah"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the same kind of question as Step 6, now about the boy.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'obligated in all the מצוות' about the boy in Step 3.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Repetition: 'וכן' already gives the boy the same status, so the phrase seems extra.

steps.title: The rule about the rebellious son is already taught elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks a possible answer. Maybe the משנה mentions the boy to teach that he can become a בן סורר ומורה? No, because that is already taught in another משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the משנה mentioned the boy because it wanted to teach 'he is fit to be a בן סורר ומורה', we already learned that once: When is he a בן סורר ומורה? From when he grows two hairs until his beard forms a circle. That means the lower hair, not the upper, but the חכמים spoke in a clean way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still pushing its question from the step before. It closes off one easy answer before anyone can give it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might say the boy's section is needed to teach about בן סורר ומורה. The גמרא says no, because a different משנה already gives that rule with its exact time window. So the question stays strong: why does our משנה spell out the boy's obligations at all?

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say. It brings up a possible answer so the גמרא can reject it.
The stubborn and rebellious son from the Torah
We already learned it once. It means the rule is already taught somewhere else.
Until the beard forms a full circle
Clean, polite language

phrases.english: And if you would say: because it wanted to teach
'and he is fit to be a stubborn and rebellious son',
we already learned it one time:
phrases.notes: This is a different משנה, in מסכת סנהדרין.

phrases.english: When is he a stubborn and rebellious son?
From when he grows two hairs
until the beard forms a circle,
the lower one and not the upper one,
but the Sages spoke in clean language!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the question of step 8 by rejecting an answer before it can be given.
steps.kashyaTarget: The extra words in the משנה about the boy being obligated in all the מצוות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The only new thing those words might add, the בן סורר ומורה rule, is already taught in another משנה, so the words still seem extra.

steps.title: The boy is described only to match the girl
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees the words about the boy aren't really needed. The משנה wrote them only because it had spelled out the girl's rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true. But since the משנה explained the details of the girl, it also explained the details of the boy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by agreeing with it. The words about the boy teach nothing new, and they are there only for balance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the girl, the extra words had a real job: they argued against רבי יוסי (step 7). For the boy, there is no new law. The משנה just keeps the two sections matching.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so. The גמרא agrees with the question.
Since, because of. It means one part was written only to match another part.
Matters, details

steps.whatToRemember: The girl's section teaches something new (against רבי יוסי). The boy's section is written only to match it.

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so,
but since it spelled out the matters of the young girl,
it also spells out the matters of the young boy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי, אֶלָּא אַיְּידֵי דְּפָרֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of steps 8-9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Agrees the words are extra and explains them as written to match the girl's section (אַיְּידֵי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every phrase in the משנה must teach a new law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The boy's obligations are repeated only to keep his section parallel to the girl's.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה about מיאון
steps.stepSummary: Going back to the משנה about a girl who grew two hairs, רבי אבהו says in the name of רבי אלעזר that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A girl who grew two hairs...' רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי אלעזר: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה from step 5 and gives a ruling on the argument there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the חכמים said two hairs end her right to do מיאון. רבי יהודה said she keeps it until the black hair is the majority. This ruling says we follow רבי יהודה, so she can still do מיאון for a longer time.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc. The rest of the quoted line is not written out.
The practical law follows this opinion

phrases.english: A young girl who grew, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from step 5 about losing the right to do מיאון.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Elazar said:
The halakha is like Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינוֹקֶת שֶׁהֵבִיאָה כּוּ׳. אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the boy/girl wording question to give a ruling on the next part of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה: a girl may do מיאון until the black hair is the majority.

steps.title: רבי יהודה agrees she loses מיאון after being with her husband
steps.stepSummary: Even רבי יהודה agrees that if she was with her husband after growing two hairs, she can no longer do מיאון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה agrees that if she was with her husband after she grew two hairs, she can no longer do מיאון.
steps.whatsHappening: This line puts a limit on the ruling we just heard. In one case, even רבי יהודה says the right to do מיאון is gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה lets her do מיאון after two hairs, but only if she has not lived with her husband since then. If she was with him after the two hairs, she can't leave through מיאון anymore. The usual explanation is that being together as an adult makes the marriage a full Torah marriage, and מיאון works only on a marriage the חכמים made for a minor.

keyTerms.meaning: And he agrees. It shows the point where the two sides agree.
She was with her husband (had relations)
To do מיאון, to refuse and end the marriage

steps.whatToRemember: We follow רבי יהודה, so she can do מיאון until the black hair is the majority. But if she was with her husband after two hairs, the right to do מיאון is gone.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda agrees
that if she was with her husband
after she grew two hairs,
she can no longer refuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling of step 11 by giving a case where even רבי יהודה agrees with the חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If she was with her husband after growing two hairs, she can no longer do מיאון, even according to רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רב כהנא's colleagues want to allow refusal even after she was with her husband
steps.stepSummary: The colleagues of רב כהנא planned to rule like רבי יהודה and let the girl do מיאון, even though she had been with her husband after growing two hairs.
steps.simpleTranslation: The colleagues of רב כהנא thought to rule in practice like רבי יהודה, even though the girl had already been with her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: Some חכמים want to go further than step 12 allowed. They want to let the girl do מיאון even after she was with her husband. This sets up רב כהנא's response in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said that once she is with her husband after growing two hairs, even רבי יהודה agrees she cannot do מיאון. The colleagues disagree and want to stretch רבי יהודה's view to cover this case too. That puts them against the ruling just taught, so רב כהנא will push back.

keyTerms.meaning: A real case; ruling in practice, not just in theory
She was with her husband (marital relations)
To act on a ruling in an actual case

phrases.english: The colleagues of Rav Kahana
thought to rule in an actual case like Rabbi Yehuda,
even though she had been with her husband.
phrases.notes: This means she was with him after growing two hairs, the exact case step 12 said even רבי יהודה does not allow.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַבְרוֹהִי דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא סְבוּר לְמֶעְבַּד עוֹבָדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a practical ruling that goes against the limit set in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The colleagues wanted to allow מיאון like רבי יהודה even after the girl was with her husband.

steps.title: רב כהנא tells the story of רבי ישמעאל's daughter
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא reminds them of a real case: רבי ישמעאל's daughter came to the בית המדרש to do מיאון with her son on her shoulders, and she wept greatly on the day her father's words were mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said to them: Didn't something like this happen with רבי ישמעאל's daughter? She came to the בית המדרש to do מיאון while her son was riding on her shoulders. That same day, רבי ישמעאל's words were mentioned in the בית המדרש, and she cried very hard in the בית המדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers his colleagues with a true story from the past. It shows what happened when a woman who already had a child came to do מיאון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The colleagues' plan matches רבי ישמעאל's view that a girl can do מיאון even after she has a child. רב כהנא brings a real case where that view was used, and it ended with great weeping. The story is a warning against ruling this way in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: A real event that happened, used as a precedent
To do מיאון, a young girl's refusal that undoes her marriage
Riding on her shoulders
The study hall, where cases were brought to the חכמים

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said to them:
Wasn't there an event just like this
with the daughter of Rabbi Yishmael,
who came to the study hall to refuse her marriage,
while her son was riding on her shoulders,
and on that very day were mentioned

phrases.aramaic: דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ,
phrases.english: the words of Rabbi Yishmael in the study hall,
and she wept a great weeping
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'and she cried' (round brackets); the corrected wording says 'and she greatly increased' her weeping (square brackets). Either way, she cried very hard.

phrases.english: in the study hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא כָּךְ הָיָה מַעֲשֶׂה בְּבִתּוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the colleagues' plan with a past case.
steps.raayaObject: That one should not rule in practice to allow מיאון after she has been with her husband.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The real event with רבי ישמעאל's daughter, who came to do מיאון with her son on her shoulders.

steps.title: The Sages react: should his own children stumble over his ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים in the בית המדרש said: Could it be that a ruling this צדיק gave would make his own descendants stumble?
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Something that this צדיק said, should his own children stumble over it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us how the חכמים reacted to the scene. They were troubled that רבי ישמעאל's own ruling was now causing trouble for his own daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל's ruling allowed a woman like her to do מיאון. But doing מיאון now meant undoing her marriage after she already had a child, which caused her great pain. The חכמים were troubled that a צדיק's own words could cause his family to stumble, and that supports רב כהנא's warning.

keyTerms.meaning: A righteous person, here meaning רבי ישמעאל
Will stumble, will be harmed
His offspring, his descendants

phrases.english: They said:
A matter that that righteous man said,
should his own offspring stumble over it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ: דָּבָר שֶׁאָמַר אוֹתוֹ צַדִּיק, יִכָּשֵׁל בּוֹ זַרְעוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story with the חכמים' reaction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים were troubled that רבי ישמעאל's own ruling was causing harm to his own descendant.

steps.title: The source of רבי ישמעאל's ruling: a mistaken betrothal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי ישמעאל's ruling. From the פסוק about סוטה, he learns that a woman whose קידושין were a mistake stays permitted, and she can do מיאון even with her son on her shoulders.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, quoting רבי ישמעאל: 'And she was not taken by force' means she is forbidden. So if she was taken by force, she is permitted. And there is another woman who is permitted even though she was not forced. Who is she? A woman whose קידושין were a mistake. Even with her son riding on her shoulders, she can do מיאון and go on her way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains which 'words of רבי ישמעאל' were mentioned in the story. It quotes his ruling and the פסוק it comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about סוטה shows that a woman who was forced stays permitted to her husband. רבי ישמעאל adds another case where she is permitted even if she was willing: a woman whose קידושין were a mistake. Since her marriage was never truly valid, she can do מיאון even after having a child, and this is exactly what his daughter tried to do.

keyTerms.meaning: She was seized, taken by force
A mistaken betrothal, one that was never truly valid
She refuses (does מיאון)
A wife suspected of being with another man

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל holds that a girl whose קידושין were a mistake can do מיאון even after having a child. רב כהנא used the story of his daughter to warn his colleagues not to rule this way in practice.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said,
Shmuel said in the name of Rabbi Yishmael:
'And she was not taken by force' — she is forbidden,
which means if she was taken by force, she is permitted,
and there is another woman

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נִתְפָּשָׂה — מוּתֶּרֶת,
phrases.english: who, even though she was not taken by force, is permitted,
and who is she?
one whose betrothal was a mistaken betrothal,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁבְּנָהּ מוּרְכָּב עַל כְּתֵפָהּ —
phrases.english: since even if her son is riding on her shoulders,
she may refuse and go on her way.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains which words of רבי ישמעאל were mentioned in the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman whose קידושין were a mistake may do מיאון even after she has a child, learned from the פסוק about סוטה.

steps.title: The Sages vote: מיאון only until two hairs
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים counted votes and ruled that a girl can do מיאון only until she grows two hairs.
steps.simpleTranslation: They counted votes and decided: Until when can a girl do מיאון? Until she grows two hairs.
steps.whatsHappening: Because of the painful story of רבי ישמעאל's daughter, the חכמים gathered, voted, and set a clear rule: a girl can do מיאון only until she grows two hairs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This vote came out of the story of a woman who had already been with her husband and had a child, and it rejects רבי ישמעאל's view that she can still do מיאון. Once she has two hairs and is then with her husband, she cannot leave through מיאון. That is why רב כהנא's colleagues, whose case was exactly this, backed down in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They counted votes and decided: a formal ruling by a vote of the חכמים
Does מיאון, a young girl's refusal that ends a marriage made for her by her mother or brothers
Two pubic hairs, the sign that a girl has become an adult

steps.whyThisMatters: This vote turns the story of רבי ישמעאל's daughter into practical הלכה. Two hairs is the cut-off for מיאון.

phrases.english: And they counted votes and decided:
Until when may a girl do refusal?
Until she grows two hairs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the result of the בית המדרש discussion about רבי ישמעאל's ruling and his weeping daughter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A girl can do מיאון only until she grows two hairs.

steps.title: רב כהנא's colleagues back down
steps.stepSummary: Hearing this, רב כהנא's colleagues pulled back and did not rule like רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They pulled back and did not act on it.
steps.whatsHappening: This closes the story from step 13: רב כהנא's colleagues, who had planned to let the girl do מיאון, backed off and did not do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא's reminder about the vote worked. His colleagues saw that the הלכה had already been decided against רבי יהודה's wider view, so they did not let the girl do מיאון.

keyTerms.meaning: They pulled back, they withdrew from their plan
Acted on it, ruled in a real, practical case

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, a girl who grew two hairs and was then with her husband cannot do מיאון. The colleagues' plan to stretch רבי יהודה's view to her case was dropped.

phrases.english: They pulled back, and did not act on it.
phrases.notes: This is about רב כהנא's colleagues from step 13. They dropped their plan to let the girl do מיאון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the effect of the vote in step 17 on the case of רב כהנא's colleagues.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice they did not follow רבי יהודה. A girl with two hairs who was with her husband cannot do מיאון.

steps.title: Another case where they followed רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק and the students of רבי חנינא did rule like רבי יהודה and let a girl do מיאון even though she had been with her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק and the students of רבי חנינא ruled in a real case like רבי יהודה, even though she had been with her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second story. Here some sages actually did let a girl with two hairs do מיאון, even after she had been with her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes even further than רבי יהודה himself. In step 12 we learned that even רבי יהודה agrees she cannot do מיאון once she was with her husband after two hairs. The phrase 'even though she was with her husband' shows how far this ruling went, and it sets up the reaction in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: She was with her husband (had relations with him)
Following the opinion of רבי יהודה in the משנה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak and the students of Rabbi Chanina
ruled in a real case like Rabbi Yehuda,
even though she had been with her husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִצְחָק וְתַלְמִידִי דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא עֲבוּד עוֹבָדָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second real case on the same question, this time where they did act like רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this case, a girl was allowed to do מיאון after two hairs, even after being with her husband.

steps.title: רבי יהודה נשיאה sends an officer to take her out
steps.stepSummary: The story went up to רבי יוחנן and then to רבי יהודה נשיאה, who sent an officer and took the girl out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמן בר אבא went and told it to רבי יוחנן. רבי יוחנן went and told it to רבי יהודה נשיאה. He sent an officer and they took her out.
steps.whatsHappening: The ruling from step 19 was reported to higher authorities, and רבי יהודה נשיאה overturned it by force, sending an officer to take the girl out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sending an officer shows that the מיאון was treated as invalid. Since she was still married to her first husband, she had to be removed from the new situation. This backs up the vote: once she was with her husband after two hairs, there is no מיאון.

keyTerms.meaning: An officer or constable sent to enforce a ruling
They took her out (removed her)
The נשיא, head of the Jewish community

steps.whatToRemember: Two stories, one message: once she has two hairs and was then with her husband, her מיאון does not work, and the leaders acted strongly to enforce this.

phrases.english: Rav Shemen bar Abba went
and told it before Rabbi Yochanan,
Rabbi Yochanan went
and told it before Rabbi Yehuda Nesia,
he sent an officer and they took her out.
phrases.notes: They took her away from the man she had married after her מיאון, because her מיאון did not count.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲזַל רַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא אַמְרַהּ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the result of the case in step 19: the ruling was overturned.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ruling like רבי יהודה was rejected in practice. The girl was removed, because her מיאון after two hairs did not work.

steps.title: מר עוקבא: what 'black outweighs white' means
steps.stepSummary: מר עוקבא explains that רבי יהודה does not mean the black hair must really outweigh the white. Two hairs lying down that look like they cover more is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of מר עוקבא: It does not mean that the black must really be more. It means that two hairs lie down and look as if the black covers more than the white.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to explaining רבי יהודה's phrase in the משנה, 'until the black outweighs the white.' מר עוקבא says it is not meant literally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read literally, רבי יהודה would require a lot of hair. מר עוקבא shrinks the requirement: two hairs long enough to lie flat, so they look like they cover more area than the bare skin. So רבי יהודה's measure is only a little more than plain 'two hairs.'

keyTerms.meaning: Black, the dark hair
White, the bare skin with no hair
Really, literally
Lying down, hairs long enough to lie flat

steps.confusionAlert: This explains how much hair רבי יהודה requires before she loses מיאון. It does not change step 12: once she is with her husband after two hairs, even רבי יהודה agrees she can no longer do מיאון.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said that Mar Ukva said:
Not that the black should really be more,
phrases.notes: He is explaining רבי יהודה's words in the משנה: 'until the black outweighs the white.'

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיוּ שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת שׁוֹכְבוֹת,
phrases.english: rather, enough that there are two hairs lying down,

phrases.aramaic: וְנִרְאוֹת כְּמִי שֶׁיִּרְבֶּה הַשָּׁחוֹר עַל הַלָּבָן.
phrases.english: and they look as if the black is more than the white.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא: לֹא שֶׁיַּרְבֶּה הַשָּׁחוֹר מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the stories to explaining the wording of רבי יהודה's view in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Black outweighs white' means two hairs lying down that look like they cover more than the skin.

steps.title: רבא: two hairs that reach from edge to edge
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different explanation: two hairs long enough to stretch across from one edge to the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Two hairs that go around from edge to edge.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second explanation of רבי יהודה's 'black outweighs white.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר עוקבא talked about hairs that lie down and look like they cover more. רבא sets a clearer measure: the two hairs must reach all the way across the area, from one edge to the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Going around, stretching across
From edge to edge

phrases.english: Rava said:
Two hairs that go around from edge to edge.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת הַמַּקִּיפוֹת מִשָּׂפָה לְשָׂפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation of the same words that מר עוקבא explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Black outweighs white' means two hairs long enough to reach from edge to edge.

steps.title: The two hairs need follicles at their roots
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the two hairs only count if there are follicles (small pits) at their roots.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חלבו said in the name of רב הונא: The two hairs that the חכמים spoke about must have follicles at their roots.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic: the details of the basic sign of two hairs. רב הונא adds a requirement that the hairs grow out of follicles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not enough to just see two hairs. They must come out of real follicles (small pits in the skin). Then we know they truly grew there and are a real sign of adulthood.

keyTerms.meaning: Follicles, small pits in the skin where hairs grow from
Their roots, the base of the hairs

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chelbo said that Rav Huna said:
The two hairs that they spoke of —
there must be follicles at their roots.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת שֶׁאָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי יהודה's measure to defining the basic two-hair sign itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two hairs only count as a sign if they have follicles at their roots.

steps.title: Follicles count even without hairs
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה says follicles alone count as the sign, even if no hairs are there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מלכיו said in the name of רב אדא בר אהבה: Follicles count, even if there are no hairs.
steps.whatsHappening: Another ruling about follicles: רב אדא בר אהבה says the follicles alone are enough to show she is an adult, even with no hairs in them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes the other way from step 23. There, follicles were needed in addition to the hairs. Here, the follicles alone are enough. The idea is that follicles don't form without hair, so hairs must have grown there and fallen out.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though there are no hairs

steps.whatToRemember: Follicles matter: hairs need them to count, and according to רב אדא בר אהבה, follicles alone are enough to show adulthood.

phrases.aramaic: רַב מַלְכִּיּוֹ אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: Rav Malkiyu said that Rav Adda bar Ahava said:

phrases.aramaic: גּוּמּוֹת, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין שְׂעָרוֹת.
phrases.english: Follicles count, even though there are no hairs.
phrases.notes: The word 'count' is not in the text; the גמרא leaves it out but means it. The follicles show that hairs were there and fell out.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מַלְכִּיּוֹ אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: גּוּמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ruling about follicles: they count as a sign even without hairs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two follicles are a sign of adulthood even if no hairs are in them.

steps.title: Which rulings belong to רב מלכיו and which to רב מלכיא
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא בריה דרב איקא lists three rulings said by רב מלכיו (skewer, maidservants, follicles) and three said by רב מלכיא (forelock, burnt ashes, cheese).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנינא son of רב איקא said: the skewer, the maidservants and the follicles rulings are from רב מלכיו. The forelock, burnt ashes and cheese rulings are from רב מלכיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The follicle rule we just learned was reported by a sage named רב מלכיו, and there is another sage with a very similar name, רב מלכיא. So the גמרא stops to list which rulings belong to which sage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a new הלכה. It is a memory list so we don't mix up two sages with nearly identical names. Each sage is given three rulings by their topic.

keyTerms.meaning: A skewer (a metal spit)
Maidservants
Follicles, small pits in the skin where hairs grow
A forelock, a lock of hair grown in front
Burnt ashes
Cheese

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חֲנִינָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chanina son of Rav Ika said:
Skewer, maidservants, and follicles: Rav Malkiyyu.
phrases.notes: Each word is a short name for a whole ruling. 'Follicles' is the rule from the last step.

phrases.aramaic: בְּלוֹרִית, אֵפֶר מִקְלֶה, וּגְבִינָה — רַב מַלְכִּיָּא.
phrases.english: Forelock, burnt ashes, and cheese: Rav Malkiyya.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חֲנִינָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Side note about who reported the follicle rule from step 24, to avoid confusing two similar names.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Skewer, maidservants and follicles belong to רב מלכיו; forelock, burnt ashes and cheese belong to רב מלכיא.

steps.title: A general rule for telling the two sages apart
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that comments on a משנה or ברייתא are from רב מלכיא, and independent statements are from רב מלכיו. Memory trick: 'the משנה is a queen.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: rulings on a משנה or a ברייתא are רב מלכיא's; independent rulings are רב מלכיו's. The memory trick is: the משנה is a queen (מלכתא).
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers a different way to sort the rulings. Instead of a list, he gives a rule based on what kind of statement it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a ruling explains a משנה or ברייתא, it belongs to רב מלכיא. If it stands on its own, it belongs to רב מלכיו. The name מלכיא sounds like מלכתא, 'queen,' and the משנה is the queen.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
A ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים outside the משנה
Independent rulings of the אמוראים
A memory sign
Queen

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Rulings on our Mishnah and on a baraita: Rav Malkiyya.
Independent rulings: Rav Malkiyyu.
And the memory sign is: the Mishnah is a queen.
phrases.notes: מלכתא sounds like מלכיא, so the queen (the משנה) goes with רב מלכיא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different sorting system from the list in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Comments on a משנה or ברייתא are רב מלכיא's; independent statements are רב מלכיו's.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two sorting systems?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רב חנינא בריה דרב איקא and רב פפא actually disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which ruling would be credited to a different sage under each system. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both systems agree on most of the rulings, so the גמרא wants to find the exact place where they give different answers.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two systems from steps 25 and 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ruling is credited to a different sage by the two systems.

steps.title: The difference is the maidservants ruling
steps.stepSummary: The two systems differ only on the ruling about maidservants.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is the maidservants ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the only ruling they credit differently is the one about maidservants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חנינא's list gives the maidservants ruling to רב מלכיו. That ruling is about a משנה, so רב פפא's rule gives it to רב מלכיא.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: Two sages with almost the same name: רב מלכיו and רב מלכיא. The follicle rule belongs to רב מלכיו. The two systems only disagree about the maidservants ruling.

phrases.english: The difference between them is maidservants.
phrases.notes: The maidservants ruling explains a משנה, so רב פפא would give it to רב מלכיא, while רב חנינא's list gives it to רב מלכיו.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They differ only on who said the maidservants ruling.

steps.title: Why didn't the משנה just mention follicles?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא מסורא asks: if follicles alone are a sign, the תנא of the משנה should have said so directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: מר זוטרא told me that רבי חנינא from סורא raised a difficulty: the תנא should not have avoided teaching us about follicles!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the follicle rule and challenges it. If follicles alone are a sign of being grown up, why does the משנה only talk about two hairs?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives 'two hairs' as the sign. If follicles without hair are enough, they would be an earlier sign, and the משנה should have taught that. Leaving them out suggests follicles alone are not a sign.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised a difficulty about it
Let him not avoid it
The teacher of the משנה
To teach us

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, אֲמַר לִי מָר זוּטְרָא,
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Mar Zutra told me,
Rabbi Chanina from Sura raised a difficulty about it:
phrases.notes: 'It' is the follicle rule from step 24.

phrases.english: Let the tanna not avoid it,
and teach us follicles!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the name discussion and returns to challenge the follicle rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that follicles alone are a sign of maturity.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה mentions only two hairs. If follicles were enough, it would have said so.

steps.title: Saying 'two hairs' teaches that even one follicle is enough
steps.stepSummary: Had the משנה said 'follicles,' we would think two hairs must be in two follicles. By saying 'two hairs,' it teaches that two hairs in one follicle also count.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it had taught us follicles, I would have said you need two hairs in two follicles. So it teaches us that even two hairs in one follicle count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The משנה chose the words 'two hairs' on purpose, to teach something that 'follicles' would not have taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Follicles' is plural, so it would suggest you need two follicles, each with a hair. By speaking about the two hairs, the משנה shows that two hairs growing from one follicle are also a sign. The follicle rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought
It teaches us
One follicle

steps.whatToRemember: Follicles alone are a sign. The משנה says 'two hairs' instead to teach that two hairs in a single follicle also count.

phrases.english: If it had taught us follicles,
I would have said: not until there are
two hairs in two follicles.
So it teaches us
that even two hairs in one follicle count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the משנה chose its wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the משנה said 'follicles,' we would require two hairs in two separate follicles.
steps.terutzMaskana: Saying 'two hairs' teaches that even two hairs in one follicle are a sign; follicles alone still count.

steps.title: Do two hairs ever grow from one follicle?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea of two hairs in one follicle by bringing a פסוק in איוב and רבא's teaching about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really such a case, two hairs in one follicle? But it is written: 'He crushes me with a storm (בשערה) and multiplies my wounds for no reason.' And רבא said: איוב insulted ה׳ with a storm, and with a storm he was answered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether two hairs can really come out of one follicle. It begins bringing a source, a פסוק in איוב with רבא's explanation, which it will unpack in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 30 depends on two hairs sharing one follicle being possible. The גמרא now doubts that this ever happens. Notice the פסוק is spelled בִּשְׂעָרָה, which looks like the word for 'hair,' while רבא reads it as סְעָרָה, 'storm.' That double meaning is where the challenge will come from.

keyTerms.meaning: a case like this
a hair
a storm, a whirlwind
he insulted, spoke harshly against ה׳
they answered him (ה׳ answered him)

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק is written with ש (שְׂעָרָה, hair), but רבא explains it as ס (סְעָרָה, storm). Keep both meanings in mind, because the גמרא will connect the 'storm' story back to hairs.

phrases.english: And is there really a case like this?
phrases.notes: He means two hairs growing out of one follicle, from Step 30.

phrases.english: But isn't it written: 'He crushes me with a storm,'
phrases.notes: איוב 9:17. The word is spelled like 'with a hair', which is the hint here.

phrases.english: 'and multiplies my wounds without cause.'
And רבא said: איוב insulted Hashem with a storm,
and with a storm he was answered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the factual basis of Step 30's answer (two hairs in one follicle).
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 30's claim that the משנה's wording covers two hairs in one follicle.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If two hairs never come from one follicle, then the משנה would have no reason to say 'two hairs' to include that case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא: איוב complained with a storm and was answered with a storm.

steps.title: How איוב complained 'with a storm'
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains איוב's complaint: perhaps a storm passed before ה׳ and He mixed up איוב with אויב (enemy).
steps.simpleTranslation: He insulted with a storm: איוב said before ה׳, 'Master of the world, maybe a storm wind passed before You, and You got confused between איוב and אויב (enemy).'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains the first half of his statement, what איוב meant by complaining 'with a storm.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: איוב suggested that ה׳ was punishing him by mistake, as if a storm caused Him to mix up two words that look almost the same: איוב and אויב. This was the 'insult.' The second half, how ה׳ answered, comes next.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: איוב claimed ה׳ confused him with an enemy, as if a storm caused the mix-up.

steps.title: How ה׳ answered 'with a storm'

steps.simpleTranslation: With a storm he was answered: 'And ה׳ answered...'

steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the second half of רבא's statement. The text breaks off mid-פסוק, so ה׳'s actual answer, which will tie back to the question about hairs, still lies ahead.
